title: Investigation of the Gut-Brain Axis in Alcohol Use Disorder
official: Investigation of the Gut-Brain Axis in Alcohol Use Disorder: A Randomized Clinical Trial on the Role of Fecal Microbiota Transplantation in Abstinence, Inflammation, and Emotional-Behavioral Regulation.
summary:
A non-profit study involving patients with moderate-to-severe Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD), designed to investigate whether correcting intestinal dysbiosis through Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) from healthy abstinent donors, combined with standard cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), improves abstinence and modulates inflammation, intestinal permeability, and neurobehavioral outcomes.

The rationale is based on preclinical evidence and clinical signals already observed in alcohol-related liver disease; however, randomized controlled trials in non-cirrhotic patients are lacking.

interventions.name: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) Procedure and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) Procedure

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Age 18-70 years; moderate-severe AUD DSM-5; recent alcohol consumption above threshold; ability to sign informed consent and adhere to protocol visits.

Exclusion Criteria:

Severe medical conditions; gastrointestinal pathologies interfering with permeability/FMT; antibiotics within the previous 4 weeks; immunodeficiency; dependence on substances other than alcohol or nicotine; serious psychiatric pathology being treated; specific pharmacotherapy for AUD; pregnancy/breastfeeding; contraindications to colonoscopy or FMT
